The failing test `testMath209()` in the `BigMatrixImplTest` class creates a `BigMatrix` instance using a 2x3 matrix and then calls the `operate` method on the matrix with a `BigDecimal` array as input.

The current bug report describes a problem in the `operate` method of `RealMatrixImpl`, which appears to be treating the input vector always with the same length as the vector itself, leading to incorrect results for non-square matrices. Looking at the code snippet for the `operate(double[] v)` method in `RealMatrixImpl`, we can see that it validates the length of the input vector `v` against the column dimension of the matrix and throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if they don't match.

The issue likely lies in the usage of `operate` in the test method `testMath209()`. The test is providing a `BigDecimal[]` input to the `operate` method, but the `operate` method is expecting a `double[]` input. This mismatch in types could lead to unexpected behavior and incorrect results, as described in the bug report.

To fix this issue, the test should provide a `double[]` input to the `operate` method instead of a `BigDecimal[]` input to match the expected input type of the method.

Next, I will suggest the best locations to apply the fix.
Suggestions for locations to fix the issue:
```
org.apache.commons.math.linear.BigMatrixImpl.operate(double[])
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
